sed_contract.addresses: None, a positive line number, $, /REGEX/ or \cREGEXc (optionally followed by I), first~step, or two addresses separated by comma; addr,+N and addr,~N extend a range; 0,/REGEX/ may end on line 1. A second regex search begins on the line after the first address matched; a numeric end at or before the start selects the start line only. Optional ! negates.

commands.d: delete pattern space and start next cycle
commands.D: delete through the first newline and restart without reading when text remains
commands.q: print (unless -n), flush appends and quit with optional exit code
commands.Q: quit with optional exit code without printing
commands.n: print (unless -n) and read the next line
commands.N: append a newline and the next line; at end of input print and exit (GNU)
commands.c: replace addressed range with text once
commands.s: s<delim>REGEX<delim>replacement<delim>[g|p|N|I|w FILE]; & whole match, \1..\9, \n, \L \U \l \u \E case conversion, escaped delimiter literal
commands.y: y/SOURCE/DEST/ transliterates equal-length byte or scalar lists
commands.H: append newline and pattern to hold
commands.G: append newline and hold to pattern
commands.t: branch if a substitution succeeded since the last input line or t
commands.l: print unambiguously, wrapped at 70 columns (l N for N)
commands.w: write pattern space to FILE through publication
commands.r: queue FILE contents for the end of the cycle (missing file reads as nothing)
commands.R: queue the next line of FILE
commands.W: write the first line of pattern space to FILE

sed_contract.multi_script: Semicolon/LF separates commands outside text, regex and escaped delimiter; -e scripts and -f files concatenate in order with newlines; braces group addressed commands; labels end at newline or semicolon. Empty script copies records.
sed_contract.in_place: -i[SUFFIX] (GNU, attached) or -i followed by an empty word (BSD) edits each file in place; SUFFIX backs up the original through the same publication, with * replaced by the file name. Each file pins its destination before its source and publishes complete output before the next file; stop on first failure, earlier files stay published.
